text: bounty — an agent-driven task board.
open [--title ..] [--timeout ..] [--no-open] [--restore ..] [--pin] [--fresh]
spawn a board daemon; prints {url, port, session_id, restoreSkipped}. --pin binds it to cwd; --session-key <key> binds it to a caller-owned key, idempotently (--fresh forces a clean board)
state [--owner ..] [--mine] [--full]          read-back: {state, cursor, readMode}; --mine | --owner <name> scope it (--full is accepted but redundant: the read is full by default — b6)
tail [--since ..] [--once] [--owner ..] [--mine]

board events as JSON lines — wrap with Monitor; it ends itself before Monitor's 30-minute cap with a line naming the next act; a human watching a terminal keeps it open with SPELLBOOK_TAIL_WINDOW_MS=0
add [title...] [--status ..] [--notes ..] [--owner ..] [--tag ..] [--size ..] [--expect ..] [--id ..] [--stdin]
add a task (the title, or --stdin); --size S|M|L is a heartbeat estimate (5/10/20 min), --expect <min> overrides it
update <id> [--status ..] [--title ..] [--notes ..] [--owner ..] [--tag ..] [--size ..] [--expect ..] [--stdin]
patch a task (--tag "" clears the tags)
claim <id>                                    self-claim an UNOWNED task as --as <name> (rejected if another owns it)
block <id> [--on ..]                          mark <id> blocked on --on <id>[,<id>...] (rejected on a cycle)
unblock <id> [--on ..]                        remove blocker edge(s) --on <id>[,<id>...]
remove <id>                                   delete a task
message [text...] [--stdin]                   show a toast on the board (the text, or --stdin)

init [--title ..] [--stdin-tasks]             seed the board (tasks = JSON array on stdin; each task REQUIRES id + title + status — init does NOT mint ids, unlike add; any dropped task is reported per-entry in tasksDropped)
close                                         end the board (writes its snapshot); prints {ok, sent, down}
info                                          the resolved board's {url, port, session_id, title}
list                                          list currently-RUNNING boards (id/tasks/url/title) — prose, see below
sessions                                      list saved SNAPSHOTS, incl. closed boards (id/tasks/title) — prose, see below
version                                       this CLI's {name, version} as JSON (alias: --version, -V)
schema                                        this CLI's machine-readable interface (acc declaration v0)
help                                          show this message (alias: --help, -h)
--help | -h | --version | -V  root tokens: help, or {name, version} as JSON
Every verb that talks to a board takes --session <id> and --session-key <key>;
those that act on it also take --as <name>. Each verb accepts only the flags
on its row.
--as <name> (or $BOUNTY_AS) is your identity — stamped on events (for scoped
tail + self-echo suppression) and used by claim/--mine. --owner assigns a task.
--stdin reads the title from stdin (verbatim — survives apostrophes, quotes,
&, <, >). Session targeting resolves --session-key <key> > --session <id> >
$BOUNTY_SESSION_KEY > $BOUNTY_SESSION > nearest .bounty-session (walking up
from cwd) > most-recent board. A --session-key is a caller-owned handle: it
derives a stable, project-scoped board id, so open --session-key K is
idempotent (attaches to a live board for K, respawns a dead one; --fresh
forces a clean one), and every verb re-derives the same id — deterministic
board binding with no stored/latest pointer. Or use open --pin to write
cwd/.bounty-session and bind a board to this directory.
Output: JSON on stdout, one document per answer — except tail (one JSON line
per event), and list, sessions and help (prose lines). Failures: one JSON
envelope on stderr, exit 2 = usage, 1 = internal, 5 = not found, 6 =
conflict. schema prints the machine-readable interface.
